steps.title: Welcome to Buildiq
steps.body: Buildiq builds apps from templates. This quick setup makes sure the bundled starter templates are available and, optionally, connects a remote template store. It is safe to run more than once.

steps.title: Install starter templates
steps.body: Fills the Store with the starter templates, so the create-from-template flow has something to offer. This normally runs on install. Run it here if OpenRegister was enabled after Buildiq, or to repair a partial install. Safe to run twice: existing templates are left untouched.

steps.title: Remote template store (optional)
steps.body: Connect a remote template catalogue to offer more starter apps. The bundled templates work without it, so leave this blank to skip.

steps.title: All set
steps.body: Buildiq is ready. Open the Store to clone a template into your first app.

steps.title: Welcome to Buildiq
steps.body: You'll create your first app from a template. Each step is yours to do. Reopen this tour anytime from the … menu.
Every app you build lives here, ready to open, edit or export.
The fastest way to start is from a template. The Store holds ready-made apps you can clone and make your own.
Cloning copies the template's schemas and pages into an app that is yours to change.
steps.task: Clone a template into a new app

steps.title: Your first app exists
steps.body: Open it from Apps to design its schemas and pages. Add your first schema next, then build a page on top of it.

pages.title: Dashboard
pages._note: Dashboard renders the self-contained DashboardIndex view (one CnDashboardPage: 4 KPI cards + Recent apps table + Quick start panel), modelled on the DocuDesk dashboard. type:custom mounts a single CnDashboardPage to avoid the dashboard-in-dashboard antipattern (hydra gate-15).

pages.title: Manifest layers
pages._note: Routed Manifest detail page (layered-versioned-app-deltas). Surfaces the three manifest customization layers (Base / Admin delta / Your delta), the per-layer OpenRegister version history + rollback (reusing VersionHistory), and the per-user create/edit/reset of the caller's own delta. type:custom mounts ManifestLayersDetail; reached from the app-detail Manifest widget. Declared before /applications/:objectId so the extra /manifest segment matches first.

config._note: Purpose-built maintainer cockpit, NOT the generic data+audit-trail archetype — deliberately exempt from the standard detail-page widget composition (detail-page-redesign brief). headerComponent/actionsComponent/slots.before-body are pre-existing, spec-driven custom components (openspec/changes/retrofit-2026-05-26-application-detail-ui): the before-body ApplicationDetailDashboard already surfaces the KPI grid, activity graph, and a Manifest/Register/Groups widget row — Register's widget already deep-links to this Application's pages/schemas/menu structure (comment in ApplicationDetailDashboard.vue: 'the schema/page/menu detail always reflects the latest manifest and is reachable from the manifest layers'), so the FK-scoped versions/pages/schemas visibility the brief calls for is already covered there, NOT duplicated here. pages and schemas are NOT OpenRegister objects (they live inside ApplicationVersion.manifest as a JSON blob) so no object-list can FK-scope them; ApplicationVersion IS a real FK child (application relation) and its history is what the sidebar 'history' tab already surfaces via rollback-capable VersionHistory. The five non-audit sidebar tabs (Manifest raw editor, Version history+rollback, Diff, Icon upload, Export jobs) are bespoke registered components (kind:'tab' in src/registry.js) with NO catalog widget equivalent (no diff/rollback/icon-upload widget type exists) — moving them into config.widgets is not expressible without inventing a widget type or registering a new kind:'widget' component, both forbidden by the manifest-only rule. Kept as-is; only the audit tab was normalised to the canonical nc-vue built-in below so History still resolves without app registration.

pages.title: Schemas
pages._note: Top-level schemas overview — renders the SchemaDesignerView (list mode) via the registry-backed `slots.default` override so the primary action is the native "Add schema" flow (SchemaListPanel + AddSchemaDialog). Previously this page was type:"index" and fell through to the generic CnIndexPage, which keys its Add button off config.schema ("application") and so mislabelled the action "Add Application". A type:"custom" + top-level `component` does NOT resolve here because CnPageRenderer (beta.107) dispatches custom pages via the empty legacy customComponents map, not the v2 registry; the slot-override path (resolvedSlotEntries) is the one that reads cnRegistry. With no :schemaId route param SchemaDesignerView renders list mode and the no-slug /schemas shortcut falls back to the hello-world app. Per-app drill-down lives under /builder/:slug/schemas.

pages.title: Store
pages._note: Templates renders the store-aware TemplateGallery view (buildiq-remote-template-store): when a registry is configured the remote store search is the primary surface with built-in templates secondary; with no registry it falls back to the built-in templates as today. Install clones via CloneTemplateDialog.

pages.title: Schemas
pages._note: Per-app schema list under the builder route — renders SchemaDesignerView (list mode, since there is no :schemaId param) via the registry-backed `slots.default` override, scoped to the virtual app identified by :slug (SchemaDesigner.vue reads `$route.params.slug`). Previously type:"index" with no slot, which fell through to the generic CnIndexPage keyed on config.schema ("application") and so listed Applications instead of the app's schemas (buildiq#41). Mirrors the top-level `/schemas` page fix above; per-schema drill-down lives at /builder/:slug/schemas/:schemaId (SchemaDesigner, detail mode).

pages.title: App
pages._note: Virtual-app host that mounts a nested CnAppRoot rendering the virtual app's own manifest from GET /api/applications/{slug}/manifest. This is a meta-app-shell (app inside app) pattern that no standard page type supports. It is the core runtime surface of buildiq and will always require a custom host component.
